source_documents.title: Reversible Thermochromism of Aggregation-Induced Emission-Active Benzophenone Azine Based on Polymorph-Dependent Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer Fluorescence

reference_evidence_units.quote: the switching between the two different polymorphs was responsible for the tunable solid fluorescence as a consequence of polymorph-dependent excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) fluorescence
a Stokes shift as large as 152 nm was observed for 1 as a result of ESIPT.
intramolecular hydrogen bonds from the salicylaldimine, which provided a structural basis for ESIPT process, were observed for both of the two polymorphs.
reference_evidence_units.statement: O-H...N hydrogen bonds in both polymorphs.

reference_evidence_units.quote: might be ascribed to the free rotations around N−N and C−C single bonds; however, in high volume fraction, rotations were inhibited because of the closely packed molecules in aggregate state, resulting in strong ESIPT fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.statement: AIE: N-N and C-C rotations quench in solution, inhibited in aggregates.

reference_evidence_units.quote: molecules in polymorph 1-Crys.(YG) packed in a much tighter mode, resulting in the fluorescence in a relative longer wavelength range.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: AIE is explained by inhibited N-N and C-C rotations in the aggregate, enabling ESIPT emission.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: Polymorph-dependent ESIPT fluorescence is the title mechanism (large Stokes shift, intramolecular H-bonds).
